pr_title: fix(core): fix memory leak caused by chrome dev tool.
pr_body:
Close #35575

In ivy, Angular attaches lView data to the DOM node, and when the DOM node is removed ,
the DOM node and the attached lView data should be garbage collected. But in Chrome,
if the chrome dev tools is opened, the last clicked dom element will be kept in the memory,
and because the DOM node holds the instance of the lView data, and the lView data holds the
component data, so a lot of data is kept in the memory which will cause memory leak and also
make memory analyze with memory snapshot difficult.

So this PR will clear the attached lView data(__ngContext__) from the DOM node when the DOM
node is detached.

pr_comments:
I agree that the current situation sucks. The issue is that chrome dev tools retains the last clicked item and with it the whole angular internal `LView`. The issue is that we can't really do much about it even if we would hide it behind `ngDevMode`. Imagine if a click removes a view, in such a situation we could clear the patched data, but 
1. it would be slow, 
2. we could do the slow part behind `ngDevMode` but
3. It would break the application. Imagine if a view is removed (we clear the patch data) and then the view is re-added. We would have to now somehow restore the data we cleared, but there is no easy way to get that data back.

So this PR is really not a feasible solution. I hear the community that this is problematic, but it is feature of chrome dev tools, and I really can't think of a way to work around this feature.

issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package The issue is caused by package @angular/core ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: .... ### Description A clear and concise description of the problem... The reproduce repo is here, https://github.com/JiaLiPassion/ivy-memory-leak Basically we have two routes with two components. `Login` and `Hello` component. 1. The homepage will redirect to `LoginComponent` ![Screenshot from 2020-02-26 07-14-29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1442575/75292500-ac12a400-5867-11ea-81a5-79f3a17572c5.png) 2. Click a button will navigate to `HelloComponent`. 3. in chrome devtools memory tab, GC->take heap snapshot, but can still find `LoginComponent` in the heap. And it is retained by an `InternalNode` object. ![Screenshot from 2020-02-26 07-15-54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1442575/75292640-ec722200-5867-11ea-9838-c7fc87470457.png) ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://github.com/JiaLiPassion/ivy-memory-leak ## 🔥 Exception or Error
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 




I assume this issue related to this one https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/35148, but I updated to the newest version `9.1.0-next.1`, but the issue still exists.
**Anything else relevant?**
comments: @JiaLiPassion just one additional question: is it only dev mode or both dev and production mode?
@pkozlowski-opensource , now it is in the dev mode, I will try the production mode now. Thanks.

@pkozlowski-opensource, it seems it also occurs in the production mode. Because in the production mode, I can not search `LoginComponent`, but I searched the `class Text`, and find the `click` text node which should only exists in the `LoginComponent`.
![Screenshot from 2020-02-20 21-12-18](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1442575/74932871-2c7b7400-5426-11ea-97e2-da7105d08093.png)

It seems the node is not detatched from the document?

thanks.

I have updated the reproduce repo, 
https://github.com/JiaLiPassion/ivy-memory-leak/tree/multi-route
maybe this is not a bug, maybe this is how chrome handle GC?
In the updated demo, there are 3 routes.
1 `Login`
2. `Hello`
3. `Hello1`

Demo steps.
1. navigate to homepage.
![Screenshot from 2020-02-25 18-38-12](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1442575/75234486-0b3bce80-57fe-11ea-9268-376cafe20e55.png)

2.  Then click button `click`, will navigate to `/hello`. Take a memory snapshot, we can find that `LoginComponent` is still in the memory, it is retained by the `app-login`  HTMLElement, and this HTMLElement has already been removed from it's parent (`app-root`), and the reason that this `app-login` HTMLElement is still in the memory is the element is retained by an `InternalNode` object, in my understanding, this `InternalNode` is ready for GC, but Chrome consider it is not necessary to destroy it at that time. 

![Screenshot from 2020-02-25 18-44-43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1442575/75234997-ef84f800-57fe-11ea-89b5-79121c9922e6.png)

3. Then click button `hello1`, will navigate to `/hello1`, Take a memory snapshot again, we can find that the `LoginComponent` is gone. And the HTMLElement `app-login` is also gone.

So maybe this is not an issue? But I tried in some more complex real project, the first component will not gone even I navigate to several other routes.

I have investigated this a bit but it seems to be something related to `RootContext` Where more than one `RootContext` objects get created and retained. (One for each login) Because they don't get released the components stay around.

If you visit the same pages over the leak stops (In other words we retain only one copy of each route, so it does not leak forever) There is definitely something fish going on here, but it is not related to https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/35148 instead it seems to be its own issue.

```

` must be set to null in order for chrome to release it. What is strange is that one would expect this to accumulate as we go back and forth between routes, but that does not seem to happen.
@JiaLiPassion Thank you for such a nice and simple repro. It makes a huge difference!

@mhevery, I create a new branch for the dom test and find something intresting.
https://github.com/JiaLiPassion/dom-memory-leak/tree/newdemo

Now the demo becomes,
1. Click `Test` button, will directly add a new button with an empty event listener.
2. and also `setTimeout` for 5 seconds to remove this new created button.

So there are two cases.
1. If I don't click the new created button, after 5 seconds, check memory snap shot, no memory leak.
2. If I click the new created button in the 5 seconds, check memory snapshot, there is memory leak.

Hello, i noticed a simliar behavior with angular 8.2. The behavior is descripted here:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60439559/angular-garbage-collection-components
Demorepo:
https://github.com/EnricoVogt/destroy_test

Should i create a own issue for this?

@JiaLiPassion Your example has me scratching my head.

See [this JSFiddle](http://jsfiddle.net/aeg8n1w2/), which is just a slightly modified version of your last code snippet.
Click "Test" then click "Remove" then take a heap snapshot of "fiddle.jshell.net".

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23387905/75721209-fb146b00-5ca5-11ea-8f5c-c7ef69817e83.png)

The "Test" class instance is still there, along with the detached `HTMLButtonElement`.
What is keeping this detached element in memory??

@JiaLiPassion, it seems Chrome keeps one instance in memory for ngFor. Memory leak isn't as severe as it would seem.

https://angular-garbage-collection-components.stackblitz.io/

By comparing snapshots on Chrome:

- clicking the last "close" it will remove the element from DOM but keep that in the memory for some odd reason.
- clicking the first "close" it will remove the element from DOM and no memory leak happens.
removing the last TestComponent by clicking "close" will leave one TestComponent in the memory.
- The TestComponent count in the memory never exceeds one over the items in the DOM.
- When I add new TestComponents the extra item is cleaned up & there is no detectable memory leak.

Code for reference: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-garbage-collection-components

The last example from @JiaLiPassion has nothing to do with Angular and it still leaks memory. So it seems like Chrome somehow keeps the last clicked item in memory for some reason. Will try to create a repro which demonstrates it. If true, than it seems to be chrome bug???

@mhevery, yeah, 
1. if the `removeChild(newCreatedButton)` happened in the event listener of the newly created button, the last clicked button will be kept.
2. if the `removeChild(newCreatedButton)` happened in the event listener of another element, nothing will be kept. 

And there are several other very strange behaviors when I test, I will post an issue in chrome. 
But for now, should we at least clear `__ngContext__` when destroy component?

review_comments: This is a megamorphic write which will happen on each destruction slowing it down. Not sure how I feel about it. @kara  and @pkozlowski-opensource what do you think?

Tend to agree with @mhevery - this is likely to slow down destroy / detach scenarios. So, as the very minimum we should run benchmarks here (existing largetable / tree would be a good start. BUT, more importantly, if we are _sure_ that this is chrome dev tools issue we should rather follow up with this team and not work-around it in Angular.

@pkozlowski-opensource , thanks and it seems Chrome will not fix this one, 
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/v8/issues/detail?id=10297#c5
Given that this happens with Chrome DevTools open and is transient, do we even need to fix it? End users will not notice anything.
It sucks if you are debugging memory leaks. Maybe can work-around under `ngDevMode`?

This pretty sucks when debugging... it's now the fourth time i've dived into debugging memory leaks because of colleagues reported to me as main Angular Developer there would be Memory Leaks and i'am not able to argue to my Team Lead why this happens and the phrase "It's just because it's dev mode" is never a accaptable answer to Senior Lead Devs!

I would also suggest to workaround with `ngDevMode` and do there some additional cleanup when Chrom won't fix it. This would save a lot of debugging time over and over again running in the same result as described above.

@mhevery @JiaLiPassion @pkozlowski-opensource hey guys. It's been 10 months since this pull request was opened. Basically, it's _mostly_ impossible to debug memory leaks in Chrome, other browsers, like Firefox or Safari, don't provide such rich functionality.

Can we give this issue a higher priority? At least as @alfaproject  proposed to invoke this function only in development mode.
